overview.headline: How seven base units are defined from fixed universal constants

keyPoints.point: Students learn the second is defined from the fixed cesium frequency value.
keyPoints.quote: The second is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the cesium frequency ∆νCs, the unperturbed ground-state hyperfine transition frequency

keyPoints.point: Students learn the meter is defined by the fixed speed of light value in vacuum.
keyPoints.quote: The meter is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the speed of light in vacuum c to be 299,792,458 when expressed in the unit m s^−1

keyPoints.point: Students learn the kilogram is defined by the fixed Planck constant value.
keyPoints.quote: The kilogram is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the Planck constant h to be 6.62607015 ×10^−34 when expressed in the unit J s

keyPoints.point: Students learn the ampere is defined by the fixed elementary charge value.
keyPoints.quote: The ampere is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the elementary charge e to be 1.602176634 × 10^−19 when expressed in the unit C

keyTerms.gloss: fixed frequency value that defines the second
keyTerms.quote: The second is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the cesium frequency ∆νCs, the unperturbed ground-state hyperfine transition frequency

keyTerms.gloss: fixed speed value that defines the meter and length
keyTerms.quote: The meter is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the speed of light in vacuum c to be 299,792,458 when expressed in the unit m s^−1

keyTerms.gloss: fixed constant value that defines the kilogram and mass
keyTerms.quote: The kilogram is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the Planck constant h to be 6.62607015 ×10^−34 when expressed in the unit J s

keyTerms.gloss: fixed charge value that defines the ampere and current
keyTerms.quote: The ampere is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the elementary charge e to be 1.602176634 × 10^−19 when expressed in the unit C

keyTerms.gloss: fixed constant value that defines the kelvin and temperature
keyTerms.quote: The kelvin is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the Boltzmann constant k to be 1.380 649 ×10^−23 when expressed in the unit J K^−1
